atoms.text: Frida Kahlo was a famous Mexican artist and painter, best known for her self-portraits. She was born on July 6th, 1907 in Mexico City. She had a German father and a Mexican mother. In 1929, Frida Kahlo married fellow artist, Diego Rivera. Throughout their life they were married twice and lived in separated homes that were connected.

Unfortunately, Frida Kahlo dealt with serious injuries and sickness throughout her life. When she was 6 years old she was diagnosed with an infectious disease called polio and was bedridden for 9 months. Later in life, she became severely injured in a bus accident. During the accident, she hurt her hip, and she spent many months in bed. Her mother placed an easel next to her bed, and Frida Kahlo began to paint.

Many of Frida Kahlo’s paintings were self-portraits. Out of the 143 paintings in total, 55 paintings were self-portraits. Frida Kahlo also liked to paint about indigenous culture, pain and politics. She was very passionate about politics and was politically active. Many of her paintings had bleeding hearts in them which symbolised pain. The Louvre, a famous art museum in Paris, France, purchased one of her paintings, which was the first time a world-famous museum purchased a painting from a Mexican artist. Frida Kahlo became popular again after she died and is remembered as an important woman in history. Her home, Casa Azul, has now been turned into a Frida Kahlo museum.
